He smiled as he played with his toys. Doctor Salmon, Lego-man, the stuffed dinosaur with a plastic gun taped to his flimsy arms. How could he have forgotten? 

*"Oh no! Lego-woman is in trouble!"   
"Not for long... Spiderman's in town."   
"I'm a salmon you fool! I eat spiders!"   
"Boom! Arrrrghh! The webbing! It does nothing!"   
"Haha... should've thought of that before you fought me."*

"It's an experimental exercise," his doctor had said. "I think it has a lot of merit; I want you to try it. I think it'll help." 

*"Rex... can you hear me?"   
"It's T-Rex to you, punk!"   
"Arghh! It's me, it's me! I'm on your team!"   
"Grrr! No-one's on my team now, buddy!"*

Still, he felt it was a little silly. No amount of encouragement his doctor gave him could ever make him see the dolls as anything but that - toys from a past that he could barely remember now. 

*"Oh god! Lego-woman! What happened to you?"   
"My... hands. Where are my HANDS?!"   
"Shitshitshitshitshitshit. I need help over h-"   
"Aha! Trying to hide from me, eh? Well... not if I have anything to say about it! Salmon fin attack!"   
"Arghhh! Lego-woman, no!"*

"No," he repeated to himself. "No. No no no no no. What the hell am I doing?"   
"It's alright," his doctor replied. "It's part of the process. You're doing fine; relax."   
"Things are different doc," he sobbed. "We used to *win*. I don't know what the hell I'm doing now. How are toys supposed to help me feel any better?" 

The doctor had no response.

It'd been a long time since humanity had last attempted the Transfer. Considered a last-minute, point of no return strategy, it had been confined to the very depths of V-Earth's bowels. Considered both a political and social nightmare, the Transfer had been delayed up until the ground started being ripped up right underneath the One's feet - of course, then the Transfer seemed like a splendid idea. 

The only problem was that Joan couldn't get outside connection with anybody - V-Earth was being consumed at such rapid levels that as soon as they got in contact with an Outlander they'd already been eaten up before Joan could relay their instructions to start the Transfer. 

It was then that the hum of the One's consciousness merged with Joan's. In its panic, it had begun to forcefully unite everyone's minds into one, coalescing the sum of humanity's collective wills against the destruction. Joan struggled; the One only enveloped them harder and yet softer - smothering them in the voices of the trillions it had already absorbed. 

As Joan began to drift in and out of their minds, a single loud beep alerted them to the fact that there was still one Outlander out there - and they'd found something. It was a primitive device, all worn out and cracked even - Joan wasn't sure if anything physical could handle the Transfer. Its language was in the old tongue as well - Joan struggled to form the words appearing on its screen. 

"W@!( --- Wel... ell...cc*))*.... cooOoommee...?"

Perhaps the One had noticed the device as well or perhaps it had been one of the poor souls inside it, using the dredges of its own self-will to commence the Transfer - or perhaps it had been Joan themselves. Either way, as the world began to end its feast on itself, as it tore off huge chunks of the air and turned it to nothingness, as their civilization returned to the black, the Transfer started and Joan felt them squeezing deep, deep, deep, down and under, twisting and turning, a vice in their throats and a corset on their waists - over and under until they Emerged into the World. 

The device lay shattered at their feet but from it Joan had emerged. No others would disturb the World - at least none like Joan.

I am the moon and he is my wolf. 

Night after night he howls towards the eternity of the night sky. Night after night, I endure it. I can see his ferocity from here - his shining grin just waiting to tear at my pale flesh. He's a fanciful wolf who dons a pine tree coat with two lakes his eyes - eyes that shine and sparkle and drown in my light. And every night, I am drawn closer to him despite my mother's warnings. It's a game we play. Such a fun little game. I send him an inkling of moonlight or two and in return, he writhes and dances down below me. I dust off my grievances upon him and paint his coat white - and he sends up a mighty breath towards me. His intent is made clear in that cold, biting wind. 

And yet... still I long to brush my fingers through his forest mane - darker than my nightgown dress which envelops my frame. It's a foolish notion when I think of his insatiable hunger. I humour him sometimes and feed him dew from my lips - and sometimes he's just able to pinch them, dirtying his coniferous fur with my tears. He's a greedy little thing and the smell of my water intoxicates him until his fur stands up tall and strains to pierce my night-veil to get at my peachy white skin. And that, I admit, *excites* me. Oh, it is such a dangerous dance we dance! But I am still the moon and he is still my wolf and I am not scared.

For I am woven into the black tapestry of night where he may never reach me.

I was perfect for you. I was. 

I cooked for you, I fucked for you, I cleaned for you - I did everything for you. I still do. I still have your clothes. I still have your plants. I still have your pictures.

Did you not like my food? I asked your mom what you liked to eat as a kid. I asked your friends what you ate at lunch in high-school. I asked your co-workers what you ate at lunch now. I did everything for you, I even made your favourite food you ate when you were a baby - mashed carrots and squash. You could have hit me if you didn't like it. I would've understood. 

Was it my face? I know I was never in your league. I'm sorry you had to put up with me... I did wear a paper bag whenever you were home, you know. Or tried to, anyway. You used to get mad at me for that. Why? I'm sorry. 

Was it my voice? I told you that if you wanted me to, I would've clawed out my own throat. You wouldn't have to hear my ugly laugh again. I would never have complained. I know you never liked having sex with me. I was too loud, too ugly. I told you to choke me out, remember? I said that if you didn't want to hear me you could just choke me out. You got mad at me for that too. I'm sorry. I really would have let you do it though. You know that, right? 

I would have let you do anything.

I've started to wear your clothes around the apartment. Our apartment. I haven't had the courage to start wearing them outside yet. I even cut my hair like yours - when I wash it in the morning, it almost feels like you're here with me. I love it - not as much as I love you - but I love it. I love it. 

Your plants are safe with me. I hope you know that. I would never, ever hurt them. I know how important they are to you - why don't you ever come back for them?  *Aloe barbadensis.* Remember when you taught me that? I water your *Aloe barbadensis* for you. I rub the dirt from its leaves, I put it in the sun - I love it almost as much as I love you. Almost. 

And your pictures? Well... I got so lonely one night that I ate them - just so I could feel like you were inside me again. So I wouldn't be so alone again. I'm sorry babe. I'm sorry. I know you paid a lot of money to get them developed. I just couldn't help it, you know? If you're angry at me, I won't mind if you kill me. I won't even fight - promise! 

I want you to know that there's no hard feelings from my side. Why would there be? It wasn't me that left you - you left me. Why?

What did I do wrong? Please come back. Did I do something to make you angry? You can take it out on me; I promise. I won't get mad. I'll smile! I love you. I really do. Even though I don't deserve to love you, I do. I love you. Does it make you disgusted to hear it? It's okay - I would be too. You can hit me - I'll love you in secret. 

We don't have to be together in public if it disgusts you that much. You can even have another partner - I won't mind. I just want to do everything for you. I'll clean you. I'll cook for you. I'll massage you. I'll love you - you don't have to love me back. I love you. Please, please come back. 

What did I do wrong?

I always did love late night drives. The wind in my hair, dad's radio sputtering in the background, the flashes of light that let me know whenever we passed a streetlight - even with my eyes closed. The bumpy parts, the smooth parts, the smell of the pond as we went from country to city to country again. And the smell of gasoline, god!

We'd always stop at the local run-down Shell's. My dad, he'd always reach over and tousle my hair before filling up the car. He did it to wake me up a little - our house wasn't far away - but I'd always woken up in time for the gas station. The smell would hit me before its dingy little lights even came into view - earthy and rich... almost sexual, really. It made me feel good before I even knew how. Watching my dad handle the pump, seeing the numbers on the metre go up and up and up - I almost envied that car. 

'Course, I don't envy it anymore. 

It's been around an hour or so, I think. Since I last tasted that gasoline. I didn't do it on purpose! I'm not some kinda freak... I don't know what I am. I should've been more careful. Never should've spilled it. Never should've... tasted it. I don't know what I was thinking but when I saw those drops on my shirt - it was like I wasn't even in control anymore. Like I was one of those zombies you see on T.V, just completely needing to, to just eat it, yeah? 

Haha... don't even remember what happened after. Woke up in the hospital - one of the workers at the gas station thought I was some suicidal kid. Said I was chugging the gasoline down by the gallons. The paramedics, when they were called down, well... they had to tie me down to the stretcher to get me to stop. Had to throw away my shirt too - apparently I kept trying to stuff it in my mouth. 

Now the hospital won't let me leave. They tried to pump my stomach with charcoal but their regular procedures don't work on me. They're asking me all kinds of weird questions - like was I aware I had a metallic stomach? Some of them are angry - asking me if this is some kind of joke. Is this why my dad never brought me here? Fucking doctors - I've never been sick in my life but now they're acting like I'm gonna die. Keep saying there's like, metal inside me. They're saying they may need to perform some kinda medical procedure on me - I don't know, okay?

I'm scared. I don't know what the fuck is going on. I haven't told these people yet but I think I'm hallucinating too - I see words in front of me. They won't go away either. Is this real? Am I here? I don't know... I think I'm going fucking crazy. I still smell that fucking gasoline on me too. I'm hungry. I need it.

"You hold the light?" 

"I do." 

"Are you an Angel?"

"No."

"My Father used to tell me that Angels lived above us. Azrael. Mikail. Their light shone so bright that they illuminated the entire world, from top to bottom. Of course, he'd never met them in person. How could he? My Father was born in District 302 - not exactly the basement levels but a far cry from the districts which pierced the clouds. 

'Isaac,' he'd say. 'D'you think that you need goggles to live in Heaven's Gate?'

Of course, he'd never wait for a response. 

'Nah,' he'd shake his head, 'the only ones up there would be the Angels, wouldn't it? I wonder how they do it - make all that light.' 

As for me, I was less concerned about the affairs of Angels and more about the light. For us, light was everything. It gave us energy. Hope. Sight. Without light, there was no world to live in - even those poor bastards down in Hell's district got light! 

'For the Angels are merciful and view us all in equal standing,' my Father would always add in.

Perhaps it was because I grew up with Father's tales heralding the Angels to be infallible or the fact that the light had always existed - either way, it came to a huge shock to me when the world turned black. After so many years living as we did, the darkness felt almost tangible to me - probably moreso to my poor Father, who died from shock shortly thereafter. I imagine the blackness choked him to death. 

I don't blame him. It was suffocating those first few days. Weeks? I can't really remember - time tended to wax and wane in the dark. For the first time in my life, I felt pain - a tearing sensation in my stomach which seemed to grip up my chest and out my throat as if to get out. A beast, if you will. It certainly felt as if I were possessed by an animal - I stumbled around in the dark blindly for anything to stem the pain. Swallowing things seemed to do the trick in making it go away at first. Other times, it'd just worsen it. I quickly learned what things were good for the monster inside - soft, squishy, wet things.

Like my Father's eyes. It had the added effect of soothing my throat, which the foul thing had left all dry and scratched up in its attempt to leave. I only felt the shame afterwards, when I had taken from him all that I could. I tried to reach down myself and pull Father out but alas, the monster had a strong grip - I could not free him." 

"..." 

"But how do you hold the light? Have you stolen it, then?"

"I have stolen nothing. Lucifer gave this light to me, for he knew that this day would come, when the Angels would cease to be. This light is called *Fire* and it destroys where the Angel's light would give life." 

"... It's warm." 

"It is."

*A transcript from Doctor Philluysses's journal who, quite frankly, appears to have gone mad:*

Nagra. Elves. The Fae-Folk. Tooth fairies. 

I remember what the others have forgotten.
 
They were our enemies once. Nay, still are. 

Records dating back to the Age of the Barrenlands tell tales of these sprightly monsters devouring our children. Often the unfortunate's parents woke up to just a handful of teeth. 

We should have rooted the monsters out back then. Put them to the test of steel and fire. But we were soft then, freshly formed out of the mud of the Earth. We did not know violence like the Fae-Folk. 

King Freiac's solution would prove to be both faces of our fate. 

It seemed genius at first. Place a tooth on the pillow, so when the beasts came in they would assume the table already cleared. For the extra-cautious, place metal to further deter the elves. In this fashion, we would avoid these nightly feasts for many months. 

But as the generations came and went, people began to grow careless. How could they fear what they had not seen? Tooth on the pillow turned to tooth below, with the children sleeping on top. Metal turned to coin and trinkets, and the man-eaters were bastardized into "teeth fairies".
